name: MO-08
label: Safe R

model.rationale: The R+27 district, Smith's overwhelming financial advantage, and prediction markets near 2% for Democrats all point to a safe Republican hold; no polls or ratings suggest movement toward the challenger.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major outside spending against Smith could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jason Smith, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win a fifth term in this southeastern Missouri district, one of the most Republican-leaning in the state at R+27. Smith has raised over $5.2 million and holds $5 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Chris Reichard has raised under $6,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Democrats only about a 2% chance of an upset.

The forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, Smith's incumbency and financial dominance, and the absence of any meaningful challenger infrastructure. The expected margin is roughly 22 points Republican, with modest uncertainty given the lack of polling.
